newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan 1997/98 capex seen down 2.1 pct--IBJ survey.
newsitem.headline: Japan 1997/98 capex seen down 2.1 pct--IBJ survey.

text.p: Capital spending by Japanese firms is expected to fall 2.1 percent next business year after an estimated 6.5 percent increase in 1996/97, a survey released on Wednesday by the Industrial Bank of Japan (IBJ) showed.

The survey of 3,222 companies conducted in late January showed that capital spending in the manufacturing sector is expected to fall 0.7 percent in 1997/98 after an estimated rise of 2.8 percent in 1996/97.
Capital spending in the non-manufacturing sector is seen dropping 2.7 percent in 1997/98 after a 7.9 percent rise in 1996/97, the survey showed.
The bank said companies are expected to revise upward their capital spending plans in the next business year starting in April, resulting in an increase in spending.
In 1995/96, overall capital spending rose 3.7 percent. Of the total, spending in manufacturing surged 12.2 percent while non-manufacturing increased 0.8 percent.

"Growth in 1997/98 capital spending is likely to be smaller than that in 1996/97 as there are concerns about a drop in semiconductor production-related spending if the market for memory chips remains sluggish for a long time," the bank said.
In the non-manufacturing sector, capital spending relating to investments in telecommunications equipment is expected to stagnate after large increases in 1996/97, it said.
